detail.longDescription: We are building a real-time AI voice platform using STT → LLM → TTS , and we are currently using Pipecat for the voice pipeline. Our main challenge is latency when handling interruptions/barge-in . When the AI is speaking and the user starts speaking, we need to stop the current TTS playback, detect/process the new speech, send it to the LLM, and start responding again. Without interruption handling the latency is acceptable, but after adding interruption/barge-in the response feels noticeably slower. What is the recommended approach to achieve low latency with Pipecat? Should we use VAD + streaming STT for interruption detection? How should we cancel/stop ongoing LLM and TTS processing? Are there specific low-latency STT, LLM, and TTS models that work well with Pipecat? Are there any architectural techniques we should use to reduce the end-to-end latency? Looking for suggestions from anyone who has built production-grade real-time voice agents with Pipecat and interruption/barge-in support.
